claim_formal: ∀ d>0: im(h_d: π_d^S → H_d(Q_0S^0;F_2)) = span_F2{h(η),h(ν),h(σ),h(θ_j) : θ_j exists, deg = d}

quote_A.text: in every positive degree, the mod-two stable Hurewicz image of the sphere is spanned by the images of η, ν, σ and the Kervaire-invariant-one classes that exist

quote_B.text: We prove Curtis's conjecture

notes: Matrix ambiguous: determination of the image as the span of an explicit generator list (M6); could be read as M7 (image = named subspace) or M1 (image ⊆ span, the reverse inclusion being classical). Prefix ∀ over degree d of a single specific map. Corollaries: Eccles's conjecture for spheres; finite image vanishing above degree 126.

claim_formal: ∀ n ∈ {1,2,…}∪{∞}: (C_n,W_n,F_n) is a proper combinatorial model structure on nCat and c_nSd²⊣Ex²N_n : sSet_KQ ⇄ nCat is a Quillen equivalence

quote_A.text: the classes $(C_n,W_n,F_n)$ in \eqref{eq:prescribed-classes} form a proper combinatorial model structure on $\nCat$

quote_B.text: We prove the higher-dimensional Thomason model-structure conjecture of Ara and Maltsiniotis.

notes: Matrix: existence of the prescribed model structure (M2) plus a Quillen equivalence (M7 component). Lean FullMain asserts Nonempty ExactModelEndpoint for n=ω and every finite n≥1, including properness, generating sets and Quillen equivalence; matches headline. n=1 (Thomason) and n=2 (Ara–Maltsiniotis) were known.

claim_formal: ∀ prime p≥5: ¬(L_2L_{K(3)}S ≃ W_3) as E(2)-local spectra (strong chromatic splitting fails at height 3); and ∀ n≥1, p>n+1: L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p admits a 2^n-stage filtration with the predicted cofibers

quote_A.text: there is no equivalence of \(E(2)\)-local spectra \(L_2L_{K(3)}S\simeq\mathcal W_3\)

quote_B.text: Disproves strong chromatic splitting at height three for primes p ≥ 5 ... Nevertheless, for n ≥ 1 and $`p\gt n+1`$, the overlap $`L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge`$ admits a $`2^n`$-stage filtration by the predicted localized-sphere pieces

notes: Family bundles: refutation of strong splitting at height 3 (p≥5); refutation of weak splitting for derived p-complete sphere at heights p and p+1; filtered replacement at generic primes; failure of finite assembly at p=n=3. O3 chosen because the refutation is paired with a corrected filtered statement; O2 also defensible. M3 vs M4: the counterexample is the specific height-3 overlap spectrum violating the conjectured equivalence.

claim_formal: ∀^∞ prime p ∃ connective p-complete X of exact fp-type 2: X ∉ Thick(BP⟨2⟩_p^∧) ∧ L_2^f X ≃ L_2 X ∧ L_{T(2)}X ≃ L_{K(2)}X

quote_A.text: For every sufficiently large prime $p$, there is a connective $p$-complete spectrum $X$ of exact fp-type two such that

quote_B.text: We disprove the Hahn–Wilson conjecture at height two.

notes: Refutes the universally quantified conjecture (stated for all heights n) via height-two counterexamples; height ≤1 cases are true (Lee–Pstrągowski). Prime threshold not explicit.

claim_formal: ∃ closed connected aspherical topological 4-manifolds M,N: M ≃ N (homotopy) ∧ M ≇ N (homeo), π_1 word-hyperbolic

quote_A.text: There exist closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds $M$ and $N$ that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic.

quote_B.text: disproving the homeomorphism-existence formulation of the Borel conjecture in dimension four

notes: Second theorem: self-homotopy equivalence not homotopic to a homeomorphism. Borel conjecture is posed in all dimensions; a dimension-4 counterexample refutes the general (homeomorphism-existence) statement, hence O2 rather than O5.

claim_formal: ∃ finite connected 3-dim CW complex X: X satisfies D(2) ∧ ¬∃ finite CW complex Y of dim ≤2 with X ≃ Y

quote_A.text: There is a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex $X$ such that

quote_B.text: We give a negative answer to Wall's finite $`D(2)`$ problem.

notes: P3 because the problem appears as Problem D3 in Wall's 1979 problem list; P2 also defensible (originally Wall 1965). Example has infinite fundamental group.

claim_formal: ∀ nonzero real Banach X,Y, ∀ surjective isometry f: S_X→S_Y, ∃! real-linear surjective isometry T: X→Y with T|_{S_X}=f

quote_A.text: Every surjective isometry between the unit spheres of real Banach spaces extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry

quote_B.text: giving an affirmative solution to Tingley's problem

notes: Paper fixes the extension explicitly (radial map) and also proves uniqueness; M1 (the radial map is a linear isometry) is an alternative reading. Lean states ∃ T with the radial formula and uniqueness among linear extensions: same.

claim_formal: ∀ F∈{ℝ,ℂ}: Con(ZFC+measurable) → (ZFC ⊬ SQ_F ∧ ZFC ⊬ ¬SQ_F); via ZFC ⊢ (c real-valued measurable → SQ_F) and ZFC ⊢ (CH → ¬SQ_F)

quote_A.text: Consequently, if ZFC with a measurable cardinal is consistent, then $\SQ_{\mathbb F}$ is independent of ZFC.

quote_B.text: The separable quotient problem asks whether every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient. We prove that this statement is independent of ZFC

notes: Lean covers only the negative half (CH → ¬SQ_ℝ ∧ ¬SQ_ℂ): weaker. Corollary: SQ at density ℵ1 independent relative to Con(ZFC) alone. Prefix 'none' (closed statement about the specific sentence SQ_F; F ranges over two fields only).

claim_formal: ∃ separable real Banach X,Y ∃ bijection Ψ: X→Y, (4/21)‖s−t‖ ≤ ‖Ψs−Ψt‖ ≤ (76/25)‖s−t‖ ∧ X ≇ Y linearly

quote_A.text: There are separable real Banach spaces that are globally bi-Lipschitz equivalent but not linearly isomorphic.

quote_B.text: This gives a negative answer to the separable Banach-space Lipschitz-isomorphism problem.

notes: Question asked by Aharoni–Lindenstrauss (1978), recorded as Problem 3 in Kalton's 2008 survey (survey restatement → P2 per rule 8). Second manuscript: separable Z without linear c0 that is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to Z⊕c0 (Kalton's Problem 2), also Lean-formalized.

claim_formal: ∀ Hilbert H, ∀ A ∈ B(H), ∀ m, ∀ matrix polynomial P ∈ M_m(ℂ)[z]: ‖P[A]‖ ≤ 2 sup_{z∈W(A)} ‖P(z)‖, and 2 is optimal

quote_A.text: \|P[A]\|\le2\max_{z\in W(A)}\|P(z)\|. \end{equation} The constant two cannot be decreased uniformly over $n,m$, and $d$.

quote_B.text: We resolve the complete Crouzeix conjecture by proving the sharp constant-two numerical-range inequality for every bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space and every matrix-valued polynomial.

notes: Sharp constant with attainment → M9. Implies the scalar Crouzeix conjecture. Lean comparators cover finite-matrix version with sharpness (CompleteCrouzeix) and the Hilbert-space operator version (CrouzeixHilbert): same. Also structural results (optimal similarity κ≤2, common positive boundary representation).

claim_formal: ∀ nonzero real Banach X with AP: K(X)<∞ ⇔ (∃q<∞ C_q(X)<∞ ∧ ∃r<∞ C_r(X*)<∞)

quote_A.text: Then \(X\) is \(K\)-convex if and only if

quote_B.text: We prove the cotype–cotype conjecture under the ordinary approximation property.

notes: Conjecture is false without approximation hypotheses (Pisier 1983); Gupta–Misra–Ray state it under BAP (Conjecture 1.5) and Pisier asked to remove the exponent restriction under BAP. Proving it under AP (⊇ BAP) settles the stated BAP formulation in full, so O1; O5 possible if the conjecture is read as the unrestricted statement. Lean MainTarget: AP → (KConvex ↔ cotype ∧ dual cotype): same.

claim_formal: ∀ real Banach X: (∃p>1 X has Markov type p) → X is superreflexive (admits equivalent uniformly convex norm)

quote_A.text: Every real Banach space with Markov type $p$ for at least one $p>1$ is superreflexive.

quote_B.text: Naor asked whether a Banach space could have nontrivial Markov type without an equivalent uniformly smooth norm \cite[Question~4]{Naor}. Since equivalent uniformly smooth and uniformly convex renormings exist for precisely the superreflexive spaces \cite{Pisier}, Theorem~\ref{thm:main} answers this question negatively

notes: Outcome by wording of Naor's question ('could X have nontrivial Markov type without a uniformly smooth renorming?' → no), hence O2; the summary frames it as a positive answer, so O1 is the natural alternative. Lean states the iff (with the known converse): counted same; with the converse the result is a characterization (M5).

claim_formal: ∀ real reflexive Banach X, ∀ nonempty closed bounded convex C⊆X, ∀ nonexpansive F: C→C, ∃ x∈C: F(x)=x

quote_A.text: Every nonexpansive selfmap of a nonempty closed bounded convex subset of a real reflexive Banach space has a fixed point.

quote_B.text: This resolves the reflexive-space fixed point problem for the given norm.

notes: Corollary: commuting families have nonempty common fixed set that is a nonexpansive retract. Problem is the classical open question (attributed to Kirk) whether reflexivity implies the fixed point property.

claim_formal: ∀ a,b ≥ 1 ∃ n ∃ origin-symmetric convex body K⊂ℝ^n: log N(K,[-1,1]^n) > b·log N(([-1,1]^n)°, a^{-1}K°)

quote_A.text: For every $a,b\ge1$, there are a positive integer $n$ and an origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\R^n$ such that

quote_B.text: We disprove Pietsch's dimension-free duality conjecture for metric entropy.

notes: Counterexamples exist already with L a cube; dimension n grows with (a,b).

claim_formal: ∃ countable uniformly discrete pointed metric space M (unbounded, nonproper): F(M) has AP ∧ ∀ λ≥1, F(M) fails λ-BAP

quote_A.text: There is a countable, unbounded, nonproper pointed metric space $(M,d,o)$ such that $d(x,y)\ge1$ for distinct points and $\F(M)$ has AP but fails $\lambda$-BAP for every finite $\lambda\ge1$.

quote_B.text: answering Kalton's question negatively

notes: Kalton's question, restated as Problem 6.2 in Godefroy's survey (survey restatement → P2). Also quantitative blocks and renormings of ℓ1 with 2B_p-BAP but not p-BAP (Lean RealL1Renorming). Lean DiscreteLipschitzFree MainStatement matches headline.

claim_formal: ∃ separable reflexive real Banach X (=J*): X's norm is AMUC (avg midpoint modulus ≥ √(1+t²/12)−1) ∧ X has no equivalent AUC norm ∧ ∀k, c_X(D_k) ≥ √(1+k/12)

quote_A.text: We construct a separable reflexive real Banach space whose given norm is asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex but which admits no asymptotically uniformly convex equivalent norm.

quote_B.text: This gives a negative answer to the reflexive diamond converse for asymptotic uniform convexifiability.

notes: Extends Baudier's nonreflexive separation (AMUC renormable ≠ AUC renormable) to the reflexive setting; the problem is the reflexive form of the diamond-embedding converse (Baudier et al. proved it under unconditional asymptotic structure). Whether the reflexive question was explicitly posed is not stated in the input, hence moderate B confidence; O8 (extension of Baudier) is an alternative. Family has 7 manuscripts with many further AMUC/no-AUC examples and Daugavet moduli; Lean ForestSpace main_theorem matches headline.

claim_formal: ℓ_1 has metric Markov cotype 2: N_2(ℓ_1) ≤ 12√21 (< ∞)

quote_A.text: The real space $\ell_1$ satisfies \[ N_2(\ell_1)\leq12\sqrt{21}. \]

quote_B.text: We prove that the real Banach space ℓ1 has metric Markov cotype two, answering a question of Mendel and Naor.

notes: Matrix: the question is finiteness of N_2(ℓ1); answered with an explicit (non-optimized) upper bound, so M8; M1 (property holds) is an alternative. Corollary: Lipschitz extension from subsets of Hilbert space into ℓ1 with universal loss (Ball's extension problem for this target).

claim_formal: ∀ closed smooth Riemannian surface (M,g) ∃ C^∞ isometric immersion F: (M,g) → (ℝ^4,δ)

quote_A.text: Every closed smooth Riemannian surface $(M,g)$ admits a $C^\infty$ isometric immersion into $(\R^4,\delta_4)$

quote_B.text: This resolves the closed-surface form of the classical four-dimensional isometric-immersion problem.

notes: Gromov's recorded question concerns arbitrary smooth Riemannian surfaces (Chern, ~1950), with uncertainty about compactness; the paper settles the compact boundaryless case, so O5 by rule 6. O1 if the question is read as the closed case.

claim_formal: ∃ smooth positive-definite metric g on (-1,1)^2: ∀ open U∋0, ¬∃ C^∞ isometric immersion (U,g) → ℝ^3

quote_A.text: yet no neighborhood of the origin admits a smooth isometric immersion into Euclidean three-space

quote_B.text: This gives a negative answer to the unrestricted smooth local isometric realization problem for surfaces.

notes: Problem appears in Yau's discussion and as Problem 1.9 in Ghomi's survey; treated as P2 (survey restatement), P3 defensible. Corollary: metric can be flat to infinite order at the origin.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥3 ∃ a_n>0 ∀ closed connected oriented smooth n-manifold M ∀ smooth metric g: ∫_M (Scal_g^-)^{n/2} dV_g ≥ a_n ‖M‖

quote_A.text: there is a constant \(a_n>0\), depending only on \(n\), such that every closed connected oriented smooth \(n\)-manifold \(M\) and every smooth Riemannian metric \(g\) on \(M\) satisfy

quote_B.text: We prove the integral scalar-curvature inequality proposed by Gromov.

notes: Gromov 1986 Conjecture 3.A, Remark (B). Companion manuscript proves rational inessentiality under PSC, i.e. the Gromov–Lawson aspherical conjecture (P1/O1), flatness of nonnegative scalar curvature on aspherical manifolds, and vanishing of simplicial volume under Scal≥0. Constant a_n not explicit.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥3 ∃ C_n ∀ complete connected boundaryless (M^n,g) with −4Δ+Scal ≥ 1 ∃ continuous f: M→K, dim K ≤ n−2, ∀y diam_g f^{-1}(y) ≤ C_n

quote_A.text: admits a continuous map $f:M\to K$ to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$ such that \[ \diam_g f^{-1}(y)\le C_n\qquad(y\in K). \] In particular, $\UW_{n-2}(M,g)\le C_n$.

quote_B.text: We prove the quantitative continuous form of Gromov's scalar-curvature conjecture in every dimension n ≥ 4.

notes: Headline (summary) is the spectral strengthening of the uniform Urysohn width bound; the family also proves the pointwise Scal≥1 version (Gromov's width conjecture, n≥4) and n=3 with explicit 500/√λ, plus macroscopic dimension ≤ n−2 for universal covers of PSC manifolds (n≥2). Coded P1/O1 since the family settles Gromov's conjecture and its spectral strengthening; O8 if the spectral result is read relative to the companion uniform-width theorem. M8 (width bound) vs M2 (existence of the map) is ambiguous. Constants C_n ineffective for n≥4, explicit for n=3.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥2, κ≤0, ∀ complete simply connected (M^n,g) with Sec ≤ κ, ∀ measurable E with vol(E)<∞, P(E)<∞: P_g(E) ≥ I_{√−κ}(vol_g(E)) (sharp, equality for model balls)

quote_A.text: every finite-volume set of finite ambient perimeter has perimeter at least that of the equal-volume ball in curvature κ

quote_B.text: We resolve the generalized Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture in every dimension.

notes: M9 (sharp comparison attained by model-space balls) vs M1 (inequality between given quantities); Euclidean equality rigidity also proved. Lean comparators formalize only the companion sharp CAT(0) integral filling theorem and optimality of its coefficient, a secondary result (which implies the Euclidean Cartan–Hadamard conjecture in dim ≥3): different. Corollaries: Faber–Krahn and Saint-Venant comparisons.

claim_formal: ∀ connected noncompact complex manifold M^n: (∃ complete Kähler metric with bisectional curvature > 0) → M ≅_biholo ℂ^n

quote_A.text: If $M$ admits a smooth complete K\"ahler metric with strictly positive holomorphic bisectional curvature, then $M$ is biholomorphic to $\C^n$.

quote_B.text: This resolves Yau's uniformization conjecture positively in every complex dimension.

notes: Matrix ambiguous: uniformization = classification with a single model (M6); M7 (isomorphism to a named object) and M1 (implication) also plausible. Yau posed it as a question in his 1982 problem section; universally called a conjecture → P1 (P3 defensible).

claim_formal: ∀ n≥3 ∀ closed connected (M^n,g) with Sec<0: h_{m_L}(φ_1) = h_top(φ_1) ⇔ ∇R_g = 0 (locally symmetric)

quote_A.text: \[ h_{m_L}(\phi_1)=\htop(\phi_1) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \nabla^gR_g=0. \]

quote_B.text: This resolves Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture positively in these dimensions

notes: Surface case was proved by Katok (1982); dimensions ≥3 complete the conjecture, hence O1 with full_only_with_prior_results (O5 if read strictly as 'n≥3 only').

claim_formal: ∃ even N ∃ closed exact embedded Lagrangian L ⊂ T*(S^9×S^{N−1}): L ≅_diff S^9×S^{N−1} ∧ L not Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section

quote_A.text: the manifold $Q=S^9\times S^{N-1}$ admits a closed exact smoothly embedded Lagrangian $L\subset T^*Q$ such that $L$ is diffeomorphic to $Q$ and no compactly supported Hamiltonian isotopy carries the zero section to $L$

quote_B.text: We disprove the unrestricted nearby Lagrangian conjecture.

notes: N is 'some sufficiently large even integer' (not explicit). Uses Waldhausen tube fibration / a kernel class in π_9 of the stable tube space.

claim_formal: ∀ closed connected oriented 4-manifold X ∀ hypersymplectic ω with ∫ω_i∧ω_j=δ_ij ∃ smooth path ω(t) of hypersymplectic structures, [ω_i(t)] fixed, ω(1) hyperkähler

quote_A.text: There is a smooth family of hypersymplectic structures $\omega(t)$, $0\le t\le1$, such that

quote_B.text: This resolves Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture.

notes: Corollaries: each α_c is Kähler for some hyperkähler metric; X is diffeomorphic to K3 or T^4.

claim_formal: ∀ closed 4-manifold X, ∀ a.c.s. J on X: (∃ symplectic ω taming J) → (∃ symplectic ω' compatible with J)

quote_A.text: every smooth almost complex structure on a closed four-manifold which is tamed by a symplectic form is compatible with a symplectic form

quote_B.text: This gives a positive solution to Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture.

notes: Also characterizes the compatible cone inside the taming cone; when b2+=1 every taming class has a compatible representative. Donaldson phrased it as Question 2 in 2006 (P2 possible), but it is standardly called a conjecture.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥3, k≥1, ∀ R,R_1..R_k>0: (⊔B^{2n}(R_i) ↪_symp Int B^{2n}(R)) ⇔ (Σ R_i^n < R^n ∧ ∀i≠j R_i+R_j < R)

quote_A.text: there exists a symplectic embedding \[ \bigsqcup_{i=1}^k B^{2n}(R_i) \hookrightarrow \Int B^{2n}(R) \] if and only if

quote_B.text: Theorem~\ref{intro:main} proves that these obstructions are complete in every real dimension at least six, resolving Siegel and Yao's Conjecture~A positively

notes: Necessity (volume and Gromov two-ball obstructions) is classical; the new content is sufficiency. Lean main_theorem is the iff (BallPackingNecessity is the easy direction). Conjecture A is posed for dimension ≥6, so O1.

claim_formal: ∀ connected closed Riemannian (M,g), dim>0: inj(M,g) = diam(M,g) → (M,g) is homothetic to S^n, RP^n, CP^n, HP^n or CaP^2 (standard)

quote_A.text: then $(M,g)$ is isometric, up to multiplication of the metric by a positive constant, to a round sphere, a standard real, complex or quaternionic projective space, or the Cayley plane.

quote_B.text: We prove the metric Blaschke conjecture

notes: Sphere and RP^n cases were known (Berger, Kazdan, Weinstein, Yang); new: sharp volume comparison Vol(M) ≥ Vol(M_0) with rigidity, giving the remaining cases.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥2 ∀ smooth Riemannian metric g on S^n ∃^∞ prime closed geodesics with pairwise distinct images

quote_A.text: For every integer $n\ge2$ and every smooth Riemannian metric on the standard smooth sphere $S^n$, there are infinitely many prime closed geodesics with pairwise different images.

quote_B.text: We resolve the sphere case of the closed-geodesic infinitude problem

notes: n=2 classical (Bangert, Franks, Hingston). The infinitude problem is posed for all closed manifolds of dimension ≥2; spheres (and via corollaries spherical space forms and all closed 3-manifolds, using Perelman and Rademacher–Taimanov) are a restricted range → O5.

claim_formal: ∀ m,n≥1 ∀ open U⊂ℝ^{m+n} ∀ stationary integral m-varifold V in U: dim_H Sing V ≤ m−1 (sharp)

quote_A.text: The singular set of every stationary integral m-varifold in an open Euclidean set has Hausdorff dimension at most $`m-1`$, in every positive dimension and codimension.

quote_B.text: This sharp bound proves the Euclidean singular-set conjecture recorded by Brena, Decio, and De Lellis.

notes: Sharpness attained by two m-planes meeting along an (m−1)-plane → M9 (M8 if attainment is ignored). Companion: almost-everywhere regularity H^m(Sing V)=0, also a Brena–Decio–De Lellis conjecture, plus the round-sphere version.
